verdict: Netflix grew revenue 13% to $10.5B on higher prices and a growing ads business, and because costs rose far more slowly than sales, operating income jumped 27% to $3.3B and net income reached $2.9B.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $5.28 a year ago (both as reported, before the 10-for-1 stock split)

segments.name: United States & Canada
segments.note: The biggest and richest market — subscription streaming, plus the fast-growing ads business.

segments.name: Europe, Middle East & Africa
segments.note: The second-largest region — up 15% as reported.

segments.name: Latin America
segments.note: Cheaper plans are pulling in new households — up 8% as reported.

segments.note: Mobile-first plans in price-sensitive markets — the fastest-growing region, up 23%.

opex.note: Advertising Netflix itself and winning subscribers.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $184M on Netflix's debt, partly offset by $51M of interest and other income — a net -$133M below operating profit.
footerNote: Regional revenues are from Netflix's Q1 2025 10-Q. Figures are rounded to whole $M; the general & administrative line is shown as $422M ($421M as reported) and the tax line as $324M ($323M as reported) so the chart ties exactly to the reported $2,890M of net income.

takeaways.title: The margin keeps expanding
takeaways.text: Operating income rose 27% YoY to $3.3B — revenue grew 13% while the cost of revenues grew just 6%, so the operating margin widened from 28% a year ago to 32%.

takeaways.title: Every region grew
takeaways.text: Asia-Pacific led at +23%, EMEA rose 15%, the U.S. & Canada 9% and Latin America 8% — price rises and the young ads business did the work in every market.

takeaways.title: Cash piled up
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $2.7B, up from $2.1B a year ago, and Netflix still expected about $8B for the full year — funding $3.5B of share buybacks in the quarter and an $800M debt repayment.
